svg.title: Processes, guests, and durable data
svg.desc: Kiro owns conversation saving, compaction, and resume. The private Fabric MCP backend caches the verified workspace runtime; workspace changes can replace the runtime without changing PID. fabric.info exposes process and runtime identity. Each execution has a fresh QuickJS context. Durable revisioned workspace state is shared across chats bound to that workspace; expectedRevision detects stale state updates. Overflow artifacts are process-owned and temporary. Same-process compaction and new-process resume require real-client qualification. See docs/diagram-descriptions.md, Lifetimes.
svg.text: The lifetime determines what can be reused

g.text: Kiro CLI process · conversation owner
Kiro saves history and compacted summaries.
Kiro controls compaction and chat resume.
Fabric state does not mirror the conversation.
Fabric backend · workspace runtime
Private stdio MCP transport; verified workspace.
Root changes can replace runtime, keeping the PID.
fabric.info(): PID, mcpInstanceId, runtime generation.
One execution · fresh QuickJS guest
All guest variables end with the call.
Compiler reuse does not preserve guest state.
Every new program is checked again.
Across restarts · workspace state
Intentional facts + revisioned task progress.
Chats in the same verified workspace share data.
expectedRevision detects stale state updates.
Stored under kiro-fabric/data/fabric/.
Temporary · overflow artifacts
Process-owned data, even when stored in files.
Default idle expiry: 1 hour; quota eviction applies.
Artifact IDs are not reliable across restarts.
Same-process compaction / new-process resume
still require authenticated real-client qualification.
Restart Kiro after an installed agent update.
